name: inner_essay_vs_ai_infra_repo
positive_pole: Confessional first-person Substack essays about ambition, meaning, half-heartedness, and not disappointing yourself (Ava bookbear express, Ashley Zhang, Ask Polly).
negative_pole: GitHub READMEs for LLM inference and serving infrastructure (vLLM, llama.cpp, ComfyUI, DeepSeek-Coder, WebLLM, open-webui).
notes: Cleanest axis in the set. Likely captures overall 'prose vs codebase' as much as topic.

name: ai_safety_discourse_vs_indie_web_aesthetics
positive_pole: Long-form AI alignment and x-risk writing (LessWrong, Anthropic, Redwood, Bengio, Cold Takes, bounded-regret) arguing about scaling, control, deception, takeoff.
negative_pole: Indie-web personal sites, portfolios, bookmark managers, CSS galleries, and 'small web' showcase pages (smallweb, Neocities, Carrd, land-book, React95, Henry from Online).

name: poetry_canon_vs_startup_world
positive_pole: Canonical poems and literary-linguistic Wikipedia pages (Poetry Foundation: Eliot, Plath, Neruda, Bishop, Carson; garden-path sentences; Borges and math).
negative_pole: Startup accelerator, VC, and founder-community landing pages (South Park Commons, Sequoia Arc, a16z, Pioneer, Indie Hackers, Betaworks, Alliance, Cofounder).

name: self_optimization_advice_vs_political_economic_history
positive_pole: First-person 'how I work / how to do things' productivity and learning essays (Recurse self-directives, Neel Nanda 'actually do things', Jason Wei, vibe-coding cheatsheets, Mitchell Hashimoto's AI adoption).
negative_pole: Wikipedia and longform on political economy, corporate power, and historical injustice (Bretton Woods, Cargill, vulture funds, Blackwater, redlining, internment, Opium War, food deserts).
notes: A 'individual agency in the present' vs 'large structural forces in history' split. Very clean.

name: saas_vc_playbook_vs_creative_technologist_homepage
positive_pole: Startup operating playbooks: SaaS metrics, fundraising, equity, retention, sales pipelines (Paul Graham, Reforge, Andreessen pmarchive, forEntrepreneurs, Sacks, CodingVC).
negative_pole: Personal sites and studio pages of creative technologists / art-and-tech practitioners (Alicia Guo, Christina Lu, Max Kreminski, Carmen Guti, Tech Poetics, Midjourney Storytelling Lab, Telescope Magazine).
notes: Both poles are tech-adjacent; the split is 'how to grow a business' vs 'I make weird beautiful computational things'.

name: deep_learning_curriculum_vs_ai_relationships_culture
positive_pole: How-to-learn-a-field resources: math/physics/CS curricula, study technique, category theory primers, Feynman technique, von Neumann quotes, Tao's 'learn and relearn'.
negative_pole: Cultural and emotional reportage on AI companions, chatbots, and AI weirdness (AI girlfriends, Friend pendant, Bing gaslighting, Zvi's AI weekly, ChatGPT-broke-up-my-relationship essays).
notes: Negative pole is more thematically coherent ('AI as social/emotional phenomenon') than the high pole is 'study technique'. The split feels like 'self-directed deep learning' vs 'culture reacting to AI as relational tech'.

name: personal_about_pages_vs_web_philosophy_essays
positive_pole: Individual 'about me' / bio pages, mostly young technical researchers and grad-students with origin stories (Karpathy, Jim Fan, Alex Zhang, Sheryl Hsu, Surya Midha, Wesley Tian, Malaika; AI residency lists; Ye Qisun bio).
negative_pole: Essayistic critique of the web itself, web3, decentralization, protocols vs platforms, enshittification, Hyrum's law (Moxie on web3, Robin Sloan, Patrick Collison, Knight Columbia, lostweb, Subconscious).
notes: Slightly heterogeneous high pole (bios + a few program/resource pages), but the recurring signature is 'this is who I am' first-person profile. Long-tail bookmarks (single-bookmark personal sites) plausibly inflate this axis.

name: embodied_interdisciplinary_mission_vs_curated_link_lists
positive_pole: Mission statements and earnest essays from interdisciplinary orgs and therapists on bodies, brains, parts, community, and care (IFS Institute, Levin Lab, Tiny Blue Dot, Neural Dynamics, Maidan Tent, participatory budgeting, attachment-style therapy, urban-ag co-creation).
negative_pole: Curated lists of links/books/blogs/papers and the index pages that host them (HN, danluu, Patrick Collison bookshelf, every-programmer-should-know, software-papers, blogrolls, textfiles.com, Gwern archiving).
notes: High pole is the messiest of the 10: blends therapy-IFS, neuro orgs, civic design, refugee architecture. The unifying thread is 'organization-or-essay-with-a-mission-to-help-humans'. Long-tail org pages likely added incoherence here.

name: group_epistemics_methods_vs_ai_hardware_economics
positive_pole: Methods for collective reasoning and good-faith inquiry: ask/guess/tell culture, double-crux, intellectual humility, reasoning transparency, EA epistemics, open-data, survey design, community notes, Bellingcat-style OSINT.
negative_pole: Deep dives on GPU/compute supply chains, inference optimization, and the economics of scaling AI hardware (SemiAnalysis on Nvidia/H100/memory/Groq, Dylan Patel interviews, LLaMa.cpp internals, deep-learning efficiency guides).
notes: A few odd LOW items (Derek Sivers 'relax for the same result', Tommy Dixon on slowness) sit with the GPU posts, hinting the LOW pole may partly index 'large-scale-systems / let-it-flow' vs 'painstaking-discourse-norms', but the dominant signal is compute-economics.

name: taste_and_aesthetics_discourse_vs_systems_engineering_artifacts
positive_pole: Essays and product pages about taste, aesthetics, design culture, and creative-economy curation (Molly Mielke on copying/stealing, Reforge on TikTok's entertainment value, Goodspeed on taste, Aesthetic Inflation, corporate art critiques, Design Arena, Recraft, mockup studios, fashion-brand websites).
negative_pole: Lower-level technical artifacts and life/philosophy primers: Rust/embedded/OS tutorials, Postgres, Slurm, OpenMM, transhumanist manifestos, Epictetus, life-goals docs.
notes: The LOW pole is a grab-bag (systems code + transhumanist philosophy + Epictetus + a personal life-update essay). Best read as 'not-about-taste' with the systems-engineering cluster dominating. Long-tail single-bookmark items (Will Hathaway life update, Epictetus, life goals doc) likely diluted what would otherwise be a cleaner 'aesthetics-discourse vs systems-engineering' axis.
